Personally, I find it more comforting to believe that we are the result of random, natural processes, than that we were put here on the whim of some omniscient, omnipotent, atemporal being.

In the former: sure, there is no greater purpose, but that gives us the freedom to find purpose for ourselves; in the latter, we're just... toys in a sandbox. There is majesty and grace in having come from humble origins and learning the powers of the cosmos, a way for the universe to know itself (and I am by no means implying that the universe has agency or awareness, in itself, here). There is nothing graceful that I can see about having been fashioned by some greater power who insists on being worshiped by the things it made.

That said, while I find arguments for evolution and such convincing, that does not make them true. I would much rather suffer the crushing disappointment of the knowledge that there is a creator, if that is what really is the case, than believe something that is not so. But I have yet to see a convincing argument that a given religion's creation myth is true, or more believable than evolution: and while evolution may have holes (and probably forever will, given our inability to directly access the distant past), I think that the overall theory is sound.
